newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:

* The win by IBM's Deep Blue computer over World Chess Champion Garry Kasparov begs the question -- Can IBM's scientists show the same resolve against another tough competitor: Microsoft Corp's Bill Gates?
* Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc named American Home Products Corp executive Fred Hassan as its new president and chief executive.
* Hawaii Gov. Ben Cayetano has received $10 million from the state Legislature to promote tourism, which has been waning in the tropical paradise.
* ABCnews.com, the World Wide Web service of ABC news, is serving as a barometer of how far new media has come as a business.
* Supporters of Pacifica Radio, a left-leaning network in Berkeley, Calif., are arguing over what should go on the air and who should make those decisions.
* Altus Biologics of Cambridge, Mass., has received a patent for a method of crystallizing enzymes.
* Supermarkets in at least 10 major metropolitan areas are trying to woo customers over the Internet.
* The owner of the Internet domain name, internet.com, has sold the name of his World Wide Web site to Mecklermedia Corp for more than $100,000.
* Federal deregulation of the telephone industry could eliminate special subsidies many small phone companies now receive for serving rural areas.
* As the Internet becomes an increasing mode of commerce, a debate is emerging: Who pays and who will determine the rules?
* Cable television is battling it out for a growing market: Latin America.
